scenario.description: Start with input → Mapper → Filter → Router → TypeScript → End: CPU and allocation of the engine alone.
Start with input → Flow Invoker (a child flow with a Mapper) → End: the cost of one flow run per envelope.

Start with input → Loop (one loop per envelope, one after another; inside: Mapper → Iteration end and Continue with) → End: the cost of one iteration (a fresh inner flow, a copy of the loop state, the stop condition).

Start with input → Loop with Parallel on (100 envelopes, 10 loops at once; inside: TypeScript that waits 5 ms → Mapper → Iteration end and Continue with) → End: running loops side by side while each iteration waits (about size / 10 × 5 ms).
Start with input (ids) → HTTP Request (8 at once, 20 ms ± 10 ms, 2 % failures diverted to the error port) → Mapper → End: waiting outside and error handling.
MongoDB Pipeline ($group in the database) → Filter → Aggregate (batches of 500) → TypeScript → Sort → Limit → End: accumulators and the memory they hold.
SQL Server Query (streamed, with backpressure) → Mapper → MongoDB Upsert (batches of 500): a SQL source into a Mongo target.

Pages of up to 500 snapshots → Flow Invoker per page: Redshift Insert of keys and rows into staging (token), Wait, one Redshift Execute that swaps them into the target in a transaction. Checks the target after each run.

MongoDB Pipeline (a window, Extended JSON) → TypeScript snapshot → MongoDB Upsert (lake, batches of 100) → Flow Invoker by path, one call per document → transformer: TypeScript with project scripts → Redshift Upsert (17 columns). Checks the target and the lake after each run.

Pages of up to 500 snapshots (MB each) → TypeScript plan with project scripts → Split → Flow Invoker by path per snapshot and list (divert) → Wait holding the page → check; each call: TypeScript → Redshift Execute (DELETE + INSERT splitting the rows in SQL). Checks the tables after each run.
